protocol.labels: Each question takes one model call. Questions with more than 32 options are labelled with two-capital single-token codes (AA, AB, …) instead of letters.

quality.intervals: [estimate, 95% percentile low, high]; ECE and mean top probability are point estimates
quality.macro: mean over the 9 benchmarks of the study's per-benchmark estimates; intervals from the mean of their bootstrap replicates, re-run on the study's predictions with its resamples

deltas.fast_minus_qwen: the study's paired cluster bootstrap on its predictions and resamples

histogram.definition: share of items per equal-width top-probability bin

gpu_price.basis: electricity estimate (410 W observed, $0.27/kWh); no hardware amortization

jev.price: `jev-1.13.0`: input $0.042, output $0 per 1M tokens (https://docs.typesafe.ai/models, as of 2026-09-25)

qwen.price: `local-gpu`: GPU wall time at $0.1107 per GPU-hour (electricity estimate: 410 W x $0.00027/Wh)

fast.price: `local-gpu`: GPU wall time at $0.1107 per GPU-hour (electricity estimate: 410 W x $0.00027/Wh)

throughput.definition: items sent by the timed invocations (response-cache hits excluded) / their summed wall time (vLLM startup excluded)
throughput.jev_note: Jev's q/s is set by our client's rate limit. The runs sent one question per request, and JevClient caps request starts at max_rpm = 1,200/min (20 requests/s), which is Jev's documented limit (1,200 requests/min and 250,000 tokens/s). Jev evaluates the questions of one request in parallel, so with N questions per request its ceiling is about 20·N q/s, up to 250,000 tokens/s (about 500 q/s at 500 tokens per question). This ceiling comes from the docs; we did not measure it.
